name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates details in low-confidence areas of video frames—like motion blur or occlusions—without hallucinating artifacts, which SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner can’t do alone. The trade-off is a 15% slowdown in processing speed, but that’s acceptable since EXCAVA’s bottleneck is output quality, not speed. The upscaler’s model is stable and widely used; no risk of stale facts here.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur because it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one—it regenerates details in still frames, not across motion. A better test: run InstantX-ComfyUI’s upscaler on a 10-second clip with heavy motion blur and compare the output to a simple frame interpolation pass; if the blur remains, the tool fails its core problem. Settle it with a blind A/B test scored by motion clarity, not just upscaled detail.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner node to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets motion blur by analyzing frame sequences, not just single frames, which InstantX’s depth-aware upscaler can’t do. The trade-off is higher VRAM usage—expect a 20% bump in memory load—but the gain in temporal consistency outweighs the slowdown for EXCAVA’s core output quality.

name: Torque
text: SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner node won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting 20% more VRAM on a tool that can’t address the core problem. A better alternative: test InstantX-ComfyUI’s temporal upscaler first—it regenerates details across frames, not just within them, which directly targets motion blur. The argument settles when we compare outputs from both tools on a 10-second clip with heavy motion blur.
